title: Audit Query Builder + Role Diff Compact UI
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and prototype a compact Audit Query Builder and Role Diff viewer for the Redwood Console. Goal: let admins craft temporal and attribute-based queries, compare role snapshots (before/after), and take lightweight approval actions from the same strip without leaving the audit context. Emphasis on a compact, scannable UI for large orgs, low cognitive load filters, and clear affordances for delegated approvers.
goals: Enable admins to construct saved audit queries with combinations of actor, resource, action, time range, and workspace tags
Show a compact, paginated Role Diff panel that highlights permission additions/removals and scope changes across snapshots
Provide inline lightweight approval actions ('Confirm', 'Escalate', 'Request Change') tied to audit entries with minimal modal friction
Surface cost and risk signals adjacent to diffs when role changes impact dedicated/dedicated-capacity routing or broad model access
Ensure prototypes reflect accessibility standards (keyboard-first, screen reader labels) and scale to orgs with tens of thousands of events
acceptance_criteria: Clickable query-builder that combines AND/OR clauses and saves to user favorites (prototype link provided)
Role Diff visual shows per-permission microchips with color-coded state (added/removed/modified) and a compact legend
Approval lane appears inline for entries flagged as high-impact or requiring multiple sign-offs
Design spec includes states for empty results, noisy-event suppression, and suggested filters for common investigations
Handoff-ready frames (Figma) with annotations for engineering metrics to instrument (query latency, pagination size, event counts)
Security sign-off checklist included and flagged for product/security review
design_decisions: Favor a single-row compact diff display with expandable rows for full permission context instead of a full-screen diff modal — reduces task-switching for ops
Use persistent query chips at the top of the audit view to make saved queries discoverable and editable inline
Introduce "approver lanes" (a horizontal micro-UI) for lightweight actions to avoid modal overload when triaging many events
Show cost/risk badges derived from telemetry next to role changes that touch dedicated capacity models or broad-scoped roles
Defer integrated timeline replay (session-by-session) to a follow-up ticket — focus this epic on query + diff + actions
tradeoffs_and_risks: Compact UI reduces visible context — mitigated by an expand-to-detail action and clear affordances
Inline actions risk accidental approvals — we propose a short delay + undo snackbar for irreversible actions
Query expressiveness vs. UI complexity — initial MVP limits advanced boolean nesting to two levels to simplify controls
Showing cost signals requires slowness-tolerant telemetry joins; we will surface estimates and link to console cost dashboards rather than live attribution
